section_summary: This section covers U.S. interagency policy debates and SCAP field operations concerning agrarian reform and food crop collections in occupied Japan between late 1946 and mid-1948. It documents SWNCC and Far Eastern Commission deliberations regarding land deconcentration and the democratization of agricultural cooperatives alongside official crop statistics. Most prominently, the records detail field investigations by agricultural economist Wolf I. Ladejinsky and Political Adviser William J. Sebald across Niigata, Kagawa, Okayama, Fukuoka, Saga, and Kumamoto prefectures, analyzing land redistribution progress, unremunerative statutory cash rents, food quota pressures, and rural socio-political changes.

subfiles.about: Transmittal and detailed commentary on Wolf I. Ladejinsky's five-prefecture agricultural field report.

subfiles.summary: Transmits and evaluates Ladejinsky's report on food collections and land reform across Fukuoka, Saga, Kumamoto, Okayama, and Kagawa prefectures. It discusses farmer food hardships, critiques sake distribution as an incentive, notes unremunerative statutory cash rents, highlights farm union strength, and commends SCAP Military Government oversight.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 201: Report of Field Trip to Fukuoka, Saga, Kumamoto, Okayama and Kagawa Prefectures to Investigate Crop Collection and Land Reform

subfiles.about: Comprehensive field investigation of crop quotas, land transfers, rents, and rural politics across five prefectures.
subfiles.from: Wolf I. Ladejinsky, Civilian Consultant, NRS SCAP
subfiles.summary: Detailed memorandum for record by Wolf I. Ladejinsky reporting on his inspection of food collections and agrarian reform across Kagawa, Okayama, Fukuoka, Saga, and Kumamoto prefectures. It highlights successful quota deliveries despite depleted farm reserves, strongly criticizes excessive sake incentive allocations, and traces land acquisition and tenant sales. Furthermore, it analyzes the economic absurdity of fixed nominal cash rents, landlord eviction attempts, water right complications, the containment of communist influence, and the vital role of Military Government teams.
subfiles.title: Field Trip to Fukuoka, Saga, Kumamoto, Okayama and Kagawa Prefectures
